- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase low-end forecasts, especially for short-term (1-7d) and mid-term (8-14d) horizons.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to post-spike values.
- Forecasts show strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >1.5x historical mean, reduce by 15-30% unless sentiment supports sustained high.
- Sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 1.00) correlates with erratic forecasts; use moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is >1.2x historical 30d mean, model often overestimates; apply downward correction if sentiment is weak or flat.
- If sentiment is high but price history shows no upward trend, model may overreact; reduce forecast magnitude by 20-40% for 30d horizon.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but recent price action is flat or declining; adjust forecast upward by 10-25% if sentiment >0.67 and price history shows no breakout.
